title: Rotate a growing application log by size and keep a few old copies
summary: When an app log grows too big, copy it to a numbered backup, empty the original, and delete the oldest copy. The app keeps writing to the same file name. A small script does this for one log file, without root rights.

steps.explain: Save the script from the script section as ~/bin/app-log-rotate.sh, then make it executable.
Check the current size of the log. The script rotates only when the file is at least MAX_BYTES large.
steps.expect: A line with the size in bytes, for example 11200000 for about 11 MB.

steps.explain: Rotate the log: copy it to name.1, empty the original, and shift older copies up to KEEP. The app keeps writing to the same file name.
steps.expect: 'rotated ... kept 5 old copies', or 'no rotation needed' when the log is still small.

steps.explain: Check the result. The original should now be small or empty, and the copies should hold the old lines.
steps.expect: The original log with a small size and files ending in .1 and .2 with the old sizes.

steps.explain: Run the rotation regularly, for example from the nightly timer or a cron line, with the same arguments.

rollback.explain: Put the old lines back: join the newest copy and the current log into a new file, then check it and replace the original once the app is stopped.

warnings: The copy-then-empty method can lose lines the app writes in the moment between the copy and the empty. This is acceptable for ordinary logs, not for audit trails.
Apps that keep the log open without append mode may write zero bytes (sparse gaps) after the file is emptied. Use an app that opens its log in append mode.
Only the oldest copy beyond KEEP is deleted. Check the folder for other files with the same name pattern first.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# Rotate one log file by size: app.log -> app.log.1 -> app.log.2 ... ; keep KEEP old copies.
# Usage: app-log-rotate.sh LOG_FILE [MAX_BYTES] [KEEP]
LOG="${1:?usage: $0 LOG_FILE [MAX_BYTES] [KEEP]}"
MAX="${2:-10485760}"
KEEP="${3:-5}"
[[ -f "$LOG" ]] || { echo "no such log: $LOG" >&2; exit 1; }
SIZE=$(stat -c %s "$LOG")
if (( SIZE < MAX )); then
  echo "no rotation needed ($SIZE bytes < $MAX)"
  exit 0
fi
rm -f -- "$LOG.$KEEP"
for (( i = KEEP - 1; i >= 1; i-- )); do
  [[ -e "$LOG.$i" ]] && mv -- "$LOG.$i" "$LOG.$((i + 1))"
done
cp -- "$LOG" "$LOG.1"
: > "$LOG"
echo "rotated $LOG ($SIZE bytes), kept $KEEP old copies"
